definition: The circle of radius $1$ centred at the origin; the point on it at angle $\theta$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis is $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$, which defines sine and cosine for any angle.
The identity $\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1$, true for every angle $\theta$, which is Pythagoras' theorem for a point on the unit circle.

When you know two sides of a triangle and an angle not between them, the sine rule can give both an acute and an obtuse angle, so two, one or no triangles may fit; keep each angle whose sum with the known angle is less than $180^{\circ}$.
